Two related repos:
- andesim: /home/nick/work/andesim (branch andesim). Hybrid RISC-V simulator orchestration: C++ driver (driver/, ./andesim), QEMU TCG plugin (qemu_plugin/), runtime (runtime/), test harness (tests/, scripts/), docs.
- vsim: /home/nick/work/vsim_andesim. External vsim (SystemC+Verilator) with hybrid orchestration in src/hybrid/*.hpp, cmake/, tests/.

Known history (ground truth for what "legacy" means here — read CLAUDE.md at /home/nick/work/andesim/CLAUDE.md and git log for detail):
- The QEMU2 handback leg was REMOVED: flow is now QEMU1 -> vsim, done. Any code/option/doc still implementing or describing a QEMU2 resume/ship-back step is legacy.
- vsim used to live in-tree under verilator/ in andesim; it moved to the external repo. Anything in andesim still referencing an in-tree verilator/ path, or building vsim locally, is legacy. NOTE: andesim/CLAUDE.md itself has a stale "vsim CMake Structure" section claiming "vsim lives entirely in verilator/" — stale docs count as findings.
- QEMU also moved to an external prebuilt (QEMU_BIN_DIR); anything cloning/building QEMU in-tree is legacy.
- Semihosting/libgloss_vh: nothing in-tree links -lgloss_vh anymore; the vplat runtime replaced it. BUT asm fixtures intentionally keep a semihosting exit fallback (semihost_exit.inc) — that is NOT legacy, per CLAUDE.md.
- The shell driver was replaced by the C++ ./andesim driver as the only user-facing driver; tests/e2e.sh is still the harness used internally (NOT legacy).

Rules:
- ONLY tracked files (git ls-files). Ignore untracked/gitignored files entirely.
- include/ in andesim is a git submodule (shared ABI pinned by BOTH repos) — never propose deletions inside it. Same for vsim external/ submodules.
- Do not propose deleting anything just because it looks old — you need positive evidence it is dead: unreferenced (grep both repos), superseded, or describes removed behavior.
- Check references across BOTH repos before claiming dead (vsim scripts may call andesim files and vice versa).
- Use git log --follow on suspicious files to understand their story.
Return findings as structured data. Be precise with paths and line ranges.

You are an adversarial verifier. A finder claims this is LEGACY code safe to delete. Try hard to REFUTE it.

Finding: repo=andesim path=docs/switching_modes_tutorial.md lines=64-89, 126 kind=stale-doc
Claim: Section 1 claims 'source ./setup.sh' builds QEMU and vsim in-tree, listing artifacts build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64 and verilator/build/sim_ax45mpv_premium, and hardcodes the old checkout path /home/nick/work/hybrid_sim.
Evidence given: Both engines are external prebuilts: setup.sh only validates QEMU_BIN_DIR/VSIM_BIN_DIR from config.env (setup.sh:102-138, 'vsim is external ... not cleaned here'); verilator/ does not exist in the repo. The tutorial's exported VSIM_BIN path points into /home/nick/work/hybrid_sim (a different, older checkout), not this repo (/home/nick/work/andesim).

Repo roots: andesim=/home/nick/work/andesim, vsim=/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim.
Checks you MUST do:
1. Read the file/lines yourself — does the claim match reality?
2. grep BOTH repos (tracked files) for references: filename, function names, symbols, script names, make targets, cmake targets, doc links.
3. Check tests/e2e.sh, scripts/*, Makefiles, CMake, and CLAUDE.md/docs for indirect usage (variable-built names, glob patterns like test_*.sh runners).
4. git log --follow -5 on the file: was it recently touched for a live feature?
5. Is it an INTENTIONAL fallback/compat layer per CLAUDE.md (e.g. semihost_exit.inc)?
If ANY live reference or intentional-keep reason exists, verdict isLegacy=false. Default to false when uncertain. If true, give the exact deleteScope.

- cc-log: Lightweight system log to record all Claude Code behavior (tool use, subagent creation, compaction, permissions, session lifecycle) for analysis. Use when the user wants to enable/disable behavior logging, analyze Claude Code session logs, list saved logs, or understand Claude Code's tool usage patterns. Trigger on: "cc-log", "behavior log", "system log", "record behavior", "log enable", "log disable", "analyze log".
- iree-optimizer: Agentic per-dispatch tile-size tuner for IREE CPU codegen on RISC-V. Keeps IREE's chosen pipeline (CPUDoubleTilingExpert / CPUConvTileAndDecomposeExpert / CPUBufferOpsTileAndVectorize) and only overrides the root linalg op's lowering_config<tile_sizes = [...]>. Each round reads the best-so-far RISC-V assembly (LMUL, VLmax, register spills) to ground the next tile-size proposal; pre-compile divisibility gate ensures tiles divide their parent extents (no tail loop); a post-compile check of the IR after iree-codegen-generic-vectorization confirms no tail/masked main path. Compiles via iree_tuner.py, benchmarks on FPGA, iterates. Use whenever the user mentions tuning IREE dispatch tile sizes, agentic tile search, or wants to replace GA-based tile-size search with LLM-driven search. Trigger on "iree optimize", "optimize dispatch", "tile tune", or references to dispatch .mlir files for performance tuning.
- libnn-optimizer: Autonomous optimization workflow for libnn RISC-V neural network library functions
in the agentic_libnn_opt project. Use this skill when the user wants to optimize a
libnn function for FPGA performance, run the libnn optimization loop, validate the
optimization config, parse FPGA hardware features, extract shapes from perf test files,
or manage the optimization state machine. Trigger when: user mentions "optimize",
"libnn", "FPGA perf", "optimization loop", "validate config",
"phase gather/baseline/iterate/evaluate", "perf test", or references opt/config.toml,
opt/state.json, or any libnn function optimization task.

Use this skill whenever someone asks to generate, write, or modify a transform dialect script, transform library, codegen strategy, or tuning spec in MLIR. Also trigger when the request involves composing IR transformations for linalg ops, controlling IREE codegen pipelines via transform dialect, or replacing annotation-only configs with full transform strategies. Covers both upstream MLIR transform ops and IREE-specific extensions.

Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.

Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". Run before committing nontrivial changes. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.

Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). 1	# Switching-Mode Tutorial and Exercises
2	
3	Status: draft for review
4	Audience: engineer running the hybrid simulator for the first time
5	Scope: the 2 switching modes the repo ships, with copy-paste commands,
6	the cycle figure each one yields, and one exercise per mode.
7	
8	---
9	
10	## 0. What "switching mode" means
11	
12	The hybrid simulator runs a program across two phases:
13	
14	```
15	   QEMU1  --(state file + shared mmap)-->  vsim
16	   (fast)                                 (cycle accurate)
17	```
18	
19	A "switching mode" is the RULE that decides WHEN QEMU1 drains its
20	architectural state and hands the region of interest to vsim. vsim runs
21	that region cycle-accurately, then drains the final state. You pick
22	the rule with plugin args and vsim CLI flags; the fixture binary does not
23	have to change between modes.
24	
25	> **Two ways to invoke, one canonical.** `./andesim run` is the driver -
26	> the supported way to run a workload, and what the examples below lead
27	> with. `tests/e2e.sh` is the regression harness that wraps the same legs
28	> behind `FIXTURE=... TRIGGER_MODE=... bash tests/e2e.sh`; it adds test-only
29	> assertions (`CHECK_MCYCLE_MONOTONIC`, `EXPECT_RC`, ...) and is shown only
30	> where those diagnostics are the point. When in doubt, use `./andesim run`.
31	
32	The repo ships **2 modes**, both profiling a kernel.
33	
34	### Quick map
35	
36	| # | Mode | Profiles | Switch boundary | Cycle figure it yields |
37	|---|------|----------|-----------------|------------------------|
38	| 1 | marker | a kernel | `slti x0,x0,0x5A0` (enter) / `slti x0,x0,0x5A1` (exit) | kernel cycles |
39	| 2 | PC | a kernel | a PC / symbol address (no source edit) | kernel cycles |
40	
41	- **Kernel modes (marker, PC)** measure ONE region you choose.
42	
43	(Migration: the old M1-M8 list collapses to these 2. Old M8 - the QEMU2
44	semihosting exit - was removed with the QEMU2 phase, so every run now ends
45	at the vsim drain.)
46	
47	### Where the cycle figure comes from
48	
49	Every mode reads the same counter: `mcycle`, a little-endian `uint64` at
50	byte offset **624** in the state file (`include/hybrid/state_abi.h`). vsim
51	restores `mcycle` from QEMU1's drained value, then the RTL counts real
52	clock cycles, so the measured cycles are always a subtraction:
53	
54	```
55	cycles = mcycle(vsim drain) - mcycle(QEMU1 drain)
56	```
57	
58	The QEMU baseline cancels; only vsim's cycle-accurate delta survives. That
59	is why QEMU being functional-only (not cycle-accurate) does not taint the
60	number. marker/pc report this delta directly as the kernel cycles.
61	
62	---
63	
64	## 1. One-time prerequisites
65	
66	Build everything once. Each command is idempotent.
67	
68	```sh
69	cd /home/nick/work/hybrid_sim
70	source ./setup.sh         # qemu + vsim + plugin
71	```
72	
73	You should now have:
74	
75	| Artifact                                | Purpose                           |
76	|-----------------------------------------|-----------------------------------|
77	| `build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64`        | QEMU binary (phase 1)             |
78	| `verilator/build/sim_ax45mpv_premium`   | vsim binary (phase 2)             |
79	| `qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so`      | TCG plugin (state drainer)        |
80	| `tests/fixtures/*.elf`                  | Test fixtures (e.g. rt_c_v_matmul) |
81	
82	Common env vars (auto-detected by `./andesim` and the e2e harness;
83	override only if you keep these elsewhere):
84	
85	```sh
86	export VSIM_QEMU=/home/nick/work/hybrid_sim/build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64
87	export VSIM_PLUGIN=/home/nick/work/hybrid_sim/qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so
88	export VSIM_BIN=/home/nick/work/hybrid_sim/verilator/build/sim_ax45mpv_premium
89	```
90	
91	---
92	
93	## 2. marker mode - the default (profiles a kernel)
94	
95	### What it does
96	
97	QEMU1's plugin pattern-matches the encoding `slti x0, x0, 0x5A0` at retire
98	time. On hit it drains state to `outfile` and exits 200. vsim does the
99	same on `slti x0, x0, 0x5A1`. The markers are RISC-V HINT NOPs (rd=x0), safe on every
100	core, so the fixture binary embeds these two `slti` instructions at the
101	kernel boundaries. vsim's drain at the `slti x0, x0, 0x5A1` marker is the
102	natural tail of the run.
103	
104	### Inputs
105	
106	- Fixture ELF with `slti x0, x0, 0x5A0` and `slti x0, x0, 0x5A1` in its source.
107	  Every C-level fixture (rt_c_v_matmul, rt_c_v_regs, rt_c_matmul, etc.) has these.
108	
109	### Cycle figure
110	
111	Kernel cycles = the vsim `mcycle` delta over the region between the two
112	markers. Run with `CHECK_MCYCLE_MONOTONIC=1` and the harness prints
113	`mcycle` at both ends:
114	
115	```sh
116	FIXTURE=rt_c_v_matmul TRIGGER_MODE=marker CHECK_MCYCLE_MONOTONIC=1 TIMEOUT=120 \
117	  bash tests/e2e.sh
118	```
119	
120	Look for the two lines `qemu1: mcycle=...` and `vsim: mcycle=...`; the
121	kernel cycle count is `vsim - qemu1` (the GEMM kernel is ~22808 cycles).
122	
123	### Run it
124	
125	```sh
126	cd /home/nick/work/hybrid_sim
127	./andesim run tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul.elf --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium
128	```
129	
130	`./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker` orchestrates the QEMU1 → vsim handoff directly (driver/cmd_run.cpp). Before the final PASS line it prints the cycle figure:
131	
132	```
133	[marker window_cycles] 22808  (vsim mcycle=... - qemu mcycle=...)
134	PASS: --mode hybrid --trigger marker (rt_c_v_matmul)
135	```
136	
137	The plugin gets `outfile=<state.bin>` and nothing else - that is the marker
138	default. vsim is launched without `--hybrid-exit-pc`, so its ELF pre-scanner
139	watches for `slti x0, x0, 0x5A1` PCs at retire.
140	
141	### Exercise 1
142	
143	The `./andesim run` examples default to the GEMM, but the harness is
144	fixture-parameterized - switch from `rt_c_v_matmul` to `rt_c_matmul`
145	(a scalar matmul) to confirm:
146	
147	```sh
148	FIXTURE=rt_c_matmul TRIGGER_MODE=marker EXPECT_RC=0 CHECK_MCYCLE_MONOTONIC=1 \
149	  bash tests/e2e.sh
150	```
151	
152	Verify the last line says `[rt_c_matmul PASS] 2-phase handoff complete (QEMU 1 drain -> vsim drain)`, and note the kernel cycle delta printed just before it (smaller than the RVV GEMM's). Then read
153	`tests/fixtures/rt_c_matmul.c` and confirm where the two ROI
154	markers live (`enter_vsim()` / `exit_vsim()` helpers).
155	
156	---
157	
158	## 3. PC mode - same kernel, no source edit
159	
160	### What it does
161	
162	Same round-trip as marker mode, but the trigger is a PC value, not an opcode
163	match. The harness resolves each boundary - taken from the required
164	`--pc-start` / `--pc-end` args (env-var form: `ROI_START` / `ROI_END`) -
165	to an address (a `0x` value is used verbatim; a name is looked up with
166	`nm`, see `tests/lib/roi.sh`), then passes:
167	
168	- `enter_pc=0x<addr>` to the QEMU plugin (QEMU1 drains there)
169	- `--hybrid-exit-pc 0x<addr>` to vsim (vsim drains there)
170	
171	marker-mode matchers are bypassed; the marker instructions become
172	inert. This proves you can hand off WITHOUT modifying the source: point the
173	boundaries at any function or address the binary already has.
174	
175	### Inputs
176	
177	- Same fixture as marker mode (`rt_c_v_matmul`). Both PC boundaries are
178	  **always explicit** -- pass `--pc-start S --pc-end E` (each a symbol
179	  name or `0x` address). There is no implicit fallback to planted
180	  `_hybrid_*_pc` markers.
181	
182	### Cycle figure
183	
184	Identical to marker mode: kernel cycles = vsim `mcycle` - QEMU1 `mcycle`.
185	The boundaries differ, the measurement does not.
186	
187	### Run it
188	
189	Resolve `--pc-end` from the binary first (the Drill-down below shows how);
190	`0x<post-jal>` is a placeholder for the instruction right after the call
191	into the kernel:
192	
193	```sh
194	./andesim run tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf --mode hybrid --trigger pc --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium \
195	  --pc-start vmatmul_kernel --pc-end 0x<post-jal>   # resolve 0x<post-jal> via the Drill-down
196	```
197	
198	The same run through the regression harness (adds the monotonic-cycle
199	assertion):
200	
201	```sh
202	FIXTURE=rt_c_v_matmul TRIGGER_MODE=pc CHECK_MCYCLE_MONOTONIC=1 TIMEOUT=120 \
203	  ROI_START=vmatmul_kernel ROI_END=0x<post-jal> \
204	  bash tests/e2e.sh
205	```
206	
207	### Drill-down
208	
209	```sh
210	NM=$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-nm
211	OBJDUMP=$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump
212	ELF=tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf
213	ENTER_PC=$("$NM" --defined-only "$ELF" | awk '$3=="vmatmul_kernel"{print "0x"$1}')
214	EXIT_PC=$("$OBJDUMP" -d "$ELF" \
215	  | awk '/<main>:/{flag=1} flag&&/jal[[:space:]]+.*<vmatmul_kernel>/{getline; print "0x"$1; exit}' \
216	  | tr -d ':')
217	
218	# QEMU plugin arg
219	... -plugin libhybrid_handoff.so,outfile=$STATE,enter_pc=$ENTER_PC
220	
221	# vsim arg
222	... --hybrid-exit-pc $EXIT_PC
223	```
224	
225	### Exercise 2
226	
227	Compare exit values: run the same fixture with `TRIGGER_MODE=marker` and again
228	with `TRIGGER_MODE=pc`. Both must exit 0 and both must drain the same PC:
229	
230	```sh
231	xxd state_csr.bin | head -4
232	xxd state_pc.bin  | head -4
233	```
234	
235	The PC field is at offset 16 (`hybrid_state_v1::pc`). For most fixtures
236	`pc(marker) == pc(pc)` because both modes drain right after the entry trigger
237	retires - so they also report the same kernel cycle delta.
238	
239	---
240	
241	## 4. Attaching a debugger (--gdb)
242	
243	Pass `--gdb` to pause the simulator at startup and open a debug port:
244	
245	- `--mode fast --gdb` injects QEMU's built-in GDB stub (`-gdb tcp::1234 -S`); connect with `riscv64-unknown-elf-gdb your.elf -ex 'target remote :1234'`.
246	- `--mode cycle --gdb` resets and **halts** the hart, opens vsim's JTAG bitbang port (`9104`), waits for it, then execs `$ICEMAN` -- a GDB server -- in the foreground; connect GDB to the server's own gdb port (OpenOCD's default `1111`). Point `$ICEMAN` at a modern **OpenOCD (0.12+)**: the version bundled with Andes ICEman has a `remote_bitbang` bug against vsim. Worked example in `docs/andes_sim_demo.ipynb` ("7. Debug with GDB").
247	
248	Use `--gdb-port N` to pick a different port for either model (requires `--gdb`); for cycle this is the JTAG bitbang port, not the gdb server's port. `--gdb` is not supported with `--mode hybrid` (the two-leg pipeline cannot pause for a debugger to attach).
249	
250	---
251	
252	## 5. Running the whole suite
253	
254	### Per-mode round-trips (one ELF at a time)
255	
256	```sh
257	./andesim run tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul.elf      --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium
258	./andesim run tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf --mode hybrid --trigger pc --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium \
259	  --pc-start vmatmul_kernel --pc-end 0x<post-jal>
260	```
261	
262	Each prints a headline figure: `./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker|pc` prints `[marker window_cycles] N` or `[pc window_cycles] N`.
263	
264	### Parallel runner (scripts/run_e2e.sh)
265	
266	```sh
267	JOBS=8 bash scripts/run_e2e.sh
268	```
269	
270	Runs every e2e fixture in parallel under a FIFO job pool.
271	
272	> The e2e suite is driven from the parent repo by `scripts/run_e2e.sh`, not
273	> by CTest. The vsim submodule keeps only the hybrid-layer doctest unit
274	> tests; there is no CTest `switching-mode` label.
275	
276	> CAUTION: on this 128-core host the default `JOBS` value can saturate the
277	> box and time out. Use `JOBS=8` as a practical cap.
278	
279	---
280	
281	## 6. Switching-mode decision flow
282	
283	When you have a new workload, pick a mode like this:
284	
285	```
286	Are you profiling ONE region you can name (a kernel)?
287	  binary is yours to edit
288	      -> marker (add andesim_ROI_begin() / _end() around the kernel)
289	  not editable, but a symbol or PC marks each end
290	      -> PC    (--pc-start <sym|0xADDR> --pc-end <sym|0xADDR>;
291	                both args are required, no default)
292	```
293	
294	---
295	
296	## 7. Common failure signatures
297	
298	| Symptom                                                 | Likely cause                                                        |
299	|---------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------|
300	| `SKIP: ... not built`                                   | `source ./setup.sh` not run, or partial build                       |
301	| `QEMU 1 expected exit 200, got 0`                       | Trigger never fired (wrong mode, wrong PC target)      |
302	| `QEMU 1 expected exit 200, got 124`                     | Plugin hung -> `timeout` killed it; check the PC target     |
303	| `cannot resolve ROI start/end '<x>'`                    | PC-mode boundary `<x>` is neither a `0x` address nor a defined symbol; fix `--pc-start`/`--pc-end` (or `ROI_START`/`ROI_END`), or use marker mode |
304	| `mcycle not strictly increasing across vsim`            | vsim measured zero cycles; check the kernel/window actually ran     |
305	| Whole suite times out under scripts/run_e2e.sh          | `JOBS` too high; set `JOBS=8`                                        |
306	
307	---
308	
309	## 8. Review checklist (for the reviewer)
310	
311	Use this when sanity-checking the tutorial against the code:
312	
313	- [ ] Plugin arg names match `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c`
314	      (`outfile`, `enter_pc`).
315	- [ ] vsim flag names match `verilator/src/main.cpp`
316	      (`--resume-from-qemu`, `--handoff-out`, `--hybrid-exit-pc`,
317	      `--shared-mem-{path,size,base}`).
318	- [ ] The 2 modes are marker and PC; the end-of-program exit is described
319	      as the run tail, not as a mode.
320	- [ ] marker/pc document the kernel cycle figure as the vsim `mcycle` delta
321	      (offset 624).
322	- [ ] `mcycle`/`minstret` offsets (624 / 632) match
323	      `include/hybrid/state_abi.h` and `tests/e2e.sh`.
324	- [ ] The suite runs via `scripts/run_e2e.sh`, NOT via a CTest
325	      `switching-mode` label.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Driver: build the plugin (qemu and vsim are external, prebuilt), then add the
# external build dirs to PATH.
# Source this script to affect your current shell's PATH:
#   source ./setup.sh                       # build all
#   source ./setup.sh clean [target]        # clean vsim|plugin|all (default: all)

if [ -n "${ZSH_VERSION:-}" ]; then
  _SETUP_SRC="${(%):-%x}"
elif [ -n "${BASH_VERSION:-}" ]; then
  _SETUP_SRC="${BASH_SOURCE[0]}"
else
  _SETUP_SRC="$0"
fi

# Wrap the body in a function so strict-mode options stay local and don't
# leak into the caller's interactive shell (which would break zsh prompts
# under nounset).
_hybrid_setup_main() {
  if [ -n "${ZSH_VERSION:-}" ]; then
    emulate -L sh
    setopt err_exit no_unset pipe_fail
  else
    local -
    set -euo pipefail
  fi

  # QEMU_BIN_DIR / VSIM_BIN_DIR are NOT in this local list: they are exported
  # for the caller's shell at the end of this function, and exporting a local
  # dies at function return (the shell pops the scope, children never see it).
  local ROOT PLUGIN_DIR PLUGIN_SO CONFIG_FILE CONFIG_TEMPLATE _arch
  ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$_SETUP_SRC")" && pwd)"
  # QEMU_BIN_DIR and VSIM_BIN_DIR (the externally-built qemu-system-* and vsim
  # sim_* build directories) both come from config.env -- this project integrates
  # a prebuilt QEMU and a prebuilt external vsim; it builds neither.
  PLUGIN_DIR="$ROOT/qemu_plugin"
  PLUGIN_SO="$PLUGIN_DIR/libhybrid_handoff.so"
  CONFIG_FILE="$ROOT/config.env"
  CONFIG_TEMPLATE="$ROOT/config.env.example"

  step() { printf '\033[1;34m==>\033[0m \033[1m%s\033[0m\n' "$*"; }
  ok()   { printf '\033[1;32m[ok]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
  err()  { printf '\033[1;31m[err]\033[0m %s\n' "$*" >&2; }

  clean_vsim()   { step "vsim is external (${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-unset})"; ok "not cleaned here -- clean it in your external vsim checkout"; }
  clean_plugin() {
    step "cleaning plugin build ($PLUGIN_DIR)"
    if [ -f "$PLUGIN_DIR/Makefile" ]; then
      make -C "$PLUGIN_DIR" clean
    else
      rm -f "$PLUGIN_SO" "$PLUGIN_DIR"/*.o
    fi
    ok "plugin cleaned"
  }

  if [ "${1:-}" = "clean" ]; then
    case "${2:-all}" in
      vsim)     clean_vsim ;;
      plugin)   clean_plugin ;;
      all)      clean_vsim; clean_plugin ;;
      *)        err "usage: source $_SETUP_SRC clean [vsim|plugin|all]"; return 1 ;;
    esac
    return 0
  fi

  step "0/3 loading per-host config"
  if [ ! -f "$CONFIG_FILE" ]; then
    if [ ! -f "$CONFIG_TEMPLATE" ]; then
      err "missing $CONFIG_TEMPLATE; cannot create $CONFIG_FILE"
      return 1
    fi
    cp "$CONFIG_TEMPLATE" "$CONFIG_FILE"
    ok "created $CONFIG_FILE from template -- edit it if your toolchain lives elsewhere"
  fi
  # shellcheck source=/dev/null
  . "$CONFIG_FILE"
  if [ -z "${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}" ]; then
    err "HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN not set; check $CONFIG_FILE"
    return 1
  fi
  if [ ! -d "$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin" ]; then
    err "HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN=$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN has no bin/ directory; edit $CONFIG_FILE"
    return 1
  fi
  export HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN
  ok "HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN=$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN"

  step "1/3 locating external qemu (rv32 + rv64)"
  if [ -z "${QEMU_BIN_DIR:-}" ]; then
    err "QEMU_BIN_DIR not set; point it at your qemu-system-* build dir in $CONFIG_FILE"
    return 1
  fi
  for _arch in riscv32 riscv64; do
    if [ ! -x "$QEMU_BIN_DIR/qemu-system-$_arch" ]; then
      err "no qemu-system-$_arch under QEMU_BIN_DIR=$QEMU_BIN_DIR; build both rv32+rv64 QEMU there or edit $CONFIG_FILE"
      return 1
    fi
  done
  ok "qemu <- $QEMU_BIN_DIR/qemu-system-{riscv32,riscv64} (external, prebuilt)"

  step "2/3 locating external vsim"
  if [ -z "${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-}" ]; then
    err "VSIM_BIN_DIR not set; point it at your external vsim build dir (holding sim_* binaries) in $CONFIG_FILE"
    return 1
  fi
  if ! ls "$VSIM_BIN_DIR"/sim_* >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    err "no sim_* under VSIM_BIN_DIR=$VSIM_BIN_DIR; build vsim in your external checkout or edit $CONFIG_FILE"
    return 1
  fi
  ok "vsim <- $VSIM_BIN_DIR (external, prebuilt)"

  step "3/3 building hybrid plugin"
  if [ ! -f "$PLUGIN_DIR/Makefile" ]; then
    err "missing $PLUGIN_DIR/Makefile"
    return 1
  fi
  # Plugins build against the vendored qemu_plugin/include/qemu-plugin.h -- no
  # QEMU source tree required.
  make -C "$PLUGIN_DIR"
  ok "plugin -> $PLUGIN_SO"

  step "PATH: prepending build dirs"
  case ":$PATH:" in
    *":$QEMU_BIN_DIR:"*) ;;
    *) export PATH="$QEMU_BIN_DIR:$PATH" ;;
  esac
  case ":$PATH:" in
    *":$VSIM_BIN_DIR:"*) ;;
    *) export PATH="$VSIM_BIN_DIR:$PATH" ;;
  esac
  ok "PATH updated (this shell only)"

  step "env: exporting QEMU_BIN_DIR / VSIM_BIN_DIR / VSIM_QEMU{,32} / VSIM_PLUGIN for the driver + e2e scripts"
  export QEMU_BIN_DIR
  export VSIM_BIN_DIR
  export VSIM_QEMU="$QEMU_BIN_DIR/qemu-system-riscv64"
  export VSIM_QEMU32="$QEMU_BIN_DIR/qemu-system-riscv32"
  export VSIM_PLUGIN="$PLUGIN_SO"
  ok "QEMU_BIN_DIR=$QEMU_BIN_DIR"
  ok "VSIM_BIN_DIR=$VSIM_BIN_DIR (external vsim; the driver discovers engines here)"
  ok "VSIM_QEMU=$VSIM_QEMU"
  ok "VSIM_QEMU32=$VSIM_QEMU32"
  ok "VSIM_PLUGIN=$VSIM_PLUGIN"

  if [ -n "${BASH_VERSION:-}" ] && [ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]:-}" = "${0:-}" ]; then
    err "script was executed, not sourced - PATH change is local to this subshell"
    err "to update your shell, run: source $_SETUP_SRC"
  fi
}

> **Writing a kernel for cycle measurement (marker/PC modes):** keep the measured

> so a kernel that carries live vector values in registers across the
> boundary may be hoisted/sunk out of the measured window. See
